name: shipment_tracking
description: Track a customer's parcel by tracking_number and email: fetch live carrier status over the web, parse the JSON, then branch first on the fetch result (network/lookup failures are terminal) and then on the parcel status (delivered, out for delivery, in transit, delayed, exception/returned/lost, or unknown). Customer-facing updates end with a satisfaction question that can escalate to a human via a support ticket. The carrier base URL and the delay threshold (days) are configurable variables.

settings.action: Fetch the live carrier tracking status for the parcel. Build the request URL by combining the carrier_base_url variable (default 'http://localhost:4000/v1') with the path '/track?number=<tracking_number>', substituting the tracking_number input. Perform an HTTP GET on that URL. Record the numeric HTTP status code as the variable http_status and whether the request completed successfully (a 200 response with a non-empty body) as the boolean variable fetch_ok. If the fetch fails, times out, returns a non-200 code, or returns an empty body, set fetch_ok to false. Otherwise parse the JSON response body and extract three fields: set the variable status to the response 'status' (lowercased), the variable last_location to 'last_location', and the variable estimated_delivery to 'estimated_delivery'. If the response indicates the tracking number is not found, unrecognized, or invalid, set the boolean variable tracking_found to false; otherwise set tracking_found to true.

conditions.condition: fetch_ok is false (the fetch failed, timed out, returned a non-200 code, or returned an empty body)
tracking_found is false (the carrier does not recognize the tracking number or it is invalid)

settings.action: Route the flow based on the parcel status held in the status variable. Any status that does not match a specific branch is treated as a normal in-transit update.

conditions.condition: status is 'in transit' and estimated_delivery is more than delay_threshold_days days away from today

settings.action: Tell the customer we could not reach the carrier to look up tracking number <tracking_number> right now, and ask them to double-check the tracking number and try again later. Do not retry automatically. This ends the flow.
Tell the customer that tracking number <tracking_number> is not recognized by the carrier yet (it may take a little time to appear after shipping) and ask them to verify it. This ends the flow.
Confirm to the customer that their parcel (tracking number <tracking_number>) has been delivered. Include the delivery location from the last_location variable. Keep it warm and concise.
Tell the customer their parcel (tracking number <tracking_number>) is out for delivery and arrives today. Include the expected time from the estimated_delivery variable.

Give the customer a normal in-transit update for tracking number <tracking_number>: state it is on its way, include its current location from the last_location variable and the expected arrival from the estimated_delivery variable.

Flag this shipment as delayed because it is still in transit and its estimated_delivery is more than delay_threshold_days days away. Record the variable escalation_reason as a short delay summary (e.g. 'In transit but delayed: estimated delivery <estimated_delivery> is more than <delay_threshold_days> days away'). Then proceed to escalation.

Open a support ticket for this shipment. Summarize the tracking number <tracking_number>, the current status from the status variable, and the reason from the escalation_reason variable (if escalation_reason is empty, derive a reason from the current status, e.g. an exception/returned/lost parcel or a customer who was not satisfied). Record the created ticket id as the variable ticket_id. Then tell the customer at <email> that a human support agent will follow up about their parcel. This ends the flow.

conditions.condition: the customer answered no / they are not satisfied / they still need help

settings.action: Thank the customer for using parcel tracking and close out the conversation politely. This ends the flow.

variables.description: Input: the carrier tracking number for the parcel to look up.
Input: the customer's email address, used when a human support agent follows up.
Configurable carrier tracking API base URL. Default 'https://api.carrier.example/v1'. The fetch step appends '/track?number=<tracking_number>' to this.
Configurable delay threshold in days. Default 7. An in-transit parcel whose estimated_delivery is more than this many days away is flagged as delayed and escalated.

True only if the carrier fetch returned a 200 with a non-empty body; false on failure, timeout, non-200, or empty response. Set by fetch_status, checked first so failures never reach the status branch.
Numeric HTTP status code returned by the carrier tracking request. Set by fetch_status.
True if the carrier recognizes the tracking number; false if the response says it is not found, unrecognized, or invalid. Set by fetch_status.
Parcel status extracted from the carrier JSON (lowercased), e.g. delivered, out for delivery, in transit, exception, returned, lost. Drives the status branch.
Most recent known location of the parcel, extracted from the carrier JSON. Shown in delivery and in-transit updates.
Estimated delivery date/time extracted from the carrier JSON. Shown to the customer and used to detect delays.
Short reason a shipment is escalated to a human (delay, exception/returned/lost, or customer not satisfied). Set by flag_delayed and used by escalate.
Identifier of the support ticket created by the escalate step.
